zh.name: socgovernance
zh.caption: 案例組織：SOC、必要時升級應變與依業務影響啟動 BCP
zh.description: 這是案例組織分工示意，不是所有 SOC 的固定編制。Tier 1 與 Tier 3 為平行分工；不是每則告警都必須進入 Tier 3、重大事件應變或 BCP。SLA、NDA、AUP 是三種平行的治理文件，不是依序執行的步驟。

items.title: SOC：持續監控
items.body: 日誌、網路、端點、雲端與威脅情報

items.title: Tier 1
items.body: 驗證與分流告警

items.title: Tier 3
items.body: 深入調查與威脅獵捕

items.title: 重大事件應變
items.body: Incident Commander 協調決策與行動

items.title: BCP：維持關鍵業務
items.body: 替代程序、復原資源、業務恢復

items.title: SLA
items.body: 服務承諾

items.title: NDA
items.body: 保密義務

items.title: AUP
items.body: 使用規則

en.name: socgovernance
en.caption: Example organization: SOC, response escalation when needed and BCP activation by business impact
en.description: This example illustrates one organization, not a mandatory structure for every SOC. Tier 1 and Tier 3 have parallel responsibilities. Not every alert requires Tier 3, major incident response or BCP activation. SLA, NDA and AUP are parallel governance documents, not sequential steps.

items.title: SOC: continuous monitoring
items.body: Logs, networks, endpoints, cloud and threat intelligence

items.title: Tier 1
items.body: Validate and triage alerts

items.title: Tier 3
items.body: Advanced investigation and threat hunting

items.title: Major incident response
items.body: The Incident Commander coordinates decisions and actions

items.title: BCP: sustain critical business
items.body: Alternative procedures, recovery resources and business restoration

items.title: SLA
items.body: Service commitments

items.title: NDA
items.body: Confidentiality obligations

items.title: AUP
items.body: Rules of use

zh.name: alerttriage
zh.caption: 從安全訊號到事件判定與必要升級
zh.description: Incident Determination 依事先定義的條件確認是否宣告資安事件；異常或告警本身並不等於已確認事件。後續依事件等級及處置權限採取適當行動。

items.title: Telemetry / Logs
items.body: 收到登入時間、來源、帳號及端點資訊

items.title: Alert
items.body: 規則或分析系統標示可疑活動

items.title: Triage
items.body: 比對授權變更、帳號行為及其他日誌

items.title: Incident Determination
items.body: 依事先定義的條件確認是否宣告資安事件

items.title: Escalation / Response
items.body: 依事件等級通知適當人員並採取行動

en.name: alerttriage
en.caption: From security signals to incident determination and escalation when needed
en.description: Incident Determination uses predefined criteria to decide whether to declare an incident. An anomaly or alert alone does not establish a confirmed incident. Subsequent action follows severity and response authority.

items.title: Telemetry / Logs
items.body: Receive login time, source, account and endpoint information

items.title: Alert
items.body: Rules or analytics flag suspicious activity

items.title: Triage
items.body: Compare authorized changes, account behavior and other logs

items.title: Incident Determination
items.body: Use predefined criteria to decide whether to declare an incident

items.title: Escalation / Response
items.body: Notify appropriate personnel and act according to incident severity

zh.name: incidentcoordination
zh.caption: 事件應變指揮者與六個平行協作團隊
zh.description: 這是重大事件組織設計範例。指揮者在預先授權內協調六個團隊；團隊之間不是依序交接的六個步驟。實際權限與角色配置由企業事先建立的應變計畫決定。

items.title: Incident Commander
items.body: 事件目標、決策、升級、協調及溝通

items.title: Security / SOC
items.body: 調查攻擊、保存證據

items.title: IT / Cloud
items.body: 隔離、修復、基礎設施復原

items.title: OT / Operations
items.body: 設備安全、製程連續性

items.title: Legal / Compliance
items.body: 法遵、通報、證據要求

items.title: Business Continuity
items.body: 替代流程與持續營運

items.title: Communications
items.body: 內外部訊息與利害關係人

en.name: incidentcoordination
en.caption: Incident Commander and six parallel collaborating teams
en.description: This is an example organization for a major incident. The commander coordinates six teams within predefined authority; the teams are not six sequential handoffs. The organization’s established response plan determines actual authority and roles.

items.title: Incident Commander
items.body: Incident objectives, decisions, escalation, coordination and communication

items.title: Security / SOC
items.body: Investigate attacks and preserve evidence

items.title: IT / Cloud
items.body: Containment, remediation and infrastructure recovery

items.title: OT / Operations
items.body: Equipment safety and process continuity

items.title: Legal / Compliance
items.body: Compliance, notification and evidence requirements

items.title: Business Continuity
items.body: Alternative processes and business continuity

items.title: Communications
items.body: Internal and external messaging and stakeholders

zh.name: recoverytimeline
zh.caption: 銀行交易系統示例：RPO 15 分鐘、RTO 2 小時
zh.description: 以下數字僅供教學，是目標而非實測結果或固定法規要求。RPO 關心資料損失的時間範圍；RTO 關心恢復服務所需的時間。兩者必須分別經過備份、復原與演練驗證。線段依 15：120（1：8）呈現真正時間比例，文字獨立排列以免窄螢幕標籤重疊。 本教學例以事故點 0 作為 RTO 計時基準；實務起訖點依業務需求與復原計畫明確定義，不表示所有 NIST 情境一律從事故點起算。

items.title: 復原點｜事故前 15 分鐘（−15 min）
items.body: RPO（Recovery Point Objective）= 15 分鐘：資料復原點目標。

items.title: 事故｜0 min
items.body: 時間軸基準點：系統中斷開始。

items.title: 復原目標｜事故後 2 小時（+120 min）
items.body: RTO（Recovery Time Objective）= 2 小時：恢復所需服務能力的目標。事故到此目標之間為系統中斷及復原期間。

en.name: recoverytimeline
en.caption: Banking transaction example: RPO 15 minutes and RTO 2 hours
en.description: These values are teaching targets, not measured results or fixed regulatory requirements. RPO concerns the time window of data loss; RTO concerns time to restore service. Each requires separate backup, recovery and exercise validation. Segments show the actual 15:120 (1:8) time ratio, with labels arranged separately to avoid overlap on narrow screens. This teaching example starts the RTO clock at incident point 0. Actual start and end criteria must be defined by business needs and recovery plans; this does not imply that every NIST scenario starts the clock at the incident.

items.title: Recovery point | 15 minutes before the incident (−15 min)
items.body: RPO (Recovery Point Objective) = 15 minutes: the target point for data recovery.

items.title: Incident | 0 min
items.body: Timeline reference point: start of the system disruption.

items.title: Recovery target | 2 hours after the incident (+120 min)
items.body: RTO (Recovery Time Objective) = 2 hours: the target to restore required service capability. The interval from the incident to this target is the system disruption and recovery period.
